WMT.rationale: Walmart presents a moderately attractive case anchored by a durable, strengthening franchise and valuation that has compressed to the low end of its 1-year PE range. YoY fundamentals are solid — +7.3% revenue growth, +19.6% EPS growth, expanding gross margins (24.9% → 25.1%) and net margins (2.8% → 3.2%) — and the structural margin inflection from high-margin platform revenue (advertising +50% YoY, membership fees +15%, now ~1/3 of operating income) is a credible long-term earnings quality catalyst. The Vibe.co acquisition extends Walmart Connect into CTV advertising, reinforcing the platform thesis. PE at 40x sits at the floor of its 39–55x 1-year range, and below a simplywall.st fair ratio of 44.4x, suggesting the market has partially de-rated the stock on cautious Q2/FY27 guidance. However, QoQ momentum is deteriorating (EPS -13%, OCF -47.9%), OCF fell below net income in Q1 FY27, and the 40x absolute multiple still demands sustained double-digit growth versus a 4.4% risk-free rate — the equity risk premium remains negative. The $20B buyback authorization and 34-analyst consensus $139 target (from $115.78) provide modest support. Score sits between mildly and moderately attractive: good franchise, reasonable relative valuation, but QoQ softness and premium absolute multiple cap conviction until Q2 FY27 confirms trajectory.
